human_tolerance.notes: Not exclusively a bird of deep forest: it can be found in suburban areas where houses and other buildings are mixed into woodlands, and in the West in riparian and oak woodlands, eucalyptus groves and some residential areas. It tends to live in stands with an open subcanopy, which makes hunting easier.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: The pair builds a stick nest, sometimes including shredded bark, leaves and green sprigs, in a major fork of a large tree, and often uses the same nest year after year, refurbishing it annually with sticks in the spring. The clutch is typically three to four eggs; incubation runs 28 to 33 days, hatching is asynchronous with the first chick up to a week ahead of the last, and the female broods the hatchlings almost constantly for up to 40 days. Overall nesting success can be lower than 30 percent.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Like almost all raptors it is monogamous and territorial, and the screaming kee-aah call is heard while courting or defending territories. Courtship displays on the breeding grounds involve soaring together in broad circles while calling, or soaring and diving toward one another, and males may perform a sky-dance, soaring high and then descending in a series of stoops.

vocalizations.description: A distinctive screaming kee-aah, usually repeated three to four times, given while courting or defending territories. Both Steller's jays and blue jays sometimes habitually imitate it, which makes them difficult to distinguish from the hawk on voice alone.

conservation.note: Wikipedia's article as used here discusses nesting success and early mortality but does not quote an IUCN category in the passages read; the least-concern category is taken from Wikidata P141.

range.note: Breeding range spans eastern North America, the coast of California, and northern to northeastern-central Mexico; it is a permanent resident throughout most of its range, and eastern populations winter from southern Wisconsin, Oklahoma, Ohio and southern New England south to the Gulf Coast.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: It searches for prey while perched on a treetop or soaring over woodlands, kills by dropping onto prey from the air, soars, glides and flaps, and in clearings flies high then drops to surprise prey; Walk covers the ground work at a kill and at carrion.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The pair builds a stick nest (sometimes including shredded bark, leaves and green sprigs) in a major fork of a large tree', reused and refurbished annually.

traits.senses.note: 'Like most raptors, red-shouldered hawks have very good vision and reasonably good sense of hearing.' Only hearing has a graded value in the schema, so Med is recorded for it; vision is left unset rather than forced into a graded field the source does not fill.

traits.mass_kg.note: Wikipedia gives an average of 550 g for males and 700 g for females; the mean of those two averages is 625 g, which is the value used.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the combined male (38-58 cm) and female (47-61 cm) length ranges, 38 to 61 cm.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 90-127 cm wingspan range.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia gives no mean: it says the birds 'have lived as long as within a month of 20 years old', that 'few live half that long', and that only around half survive their first year. 10 years is taken as the value that few reach, and is close to a quarter of the record.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia states small mammals, especially rodents, are typically the most common prey - voles, gophers, mice, moles and chipmunks, with rabbits and tree squirrels occasionally taken - and that other prey includes amphibians, reptiles (especially small snakes), birds, fish and large insects. It also records prey that includes nocturnal animals and road-killed deer, and that the hawk may cache food near its nest. The 80/10/10 split across vertebrate, invertebrate and carrion is authored judgement within that description.

traits.social.note: 'Like almost all raptors, the red-shouldered hawk is monogamous and territorial.'

traits.activity_pattern.note: It hunts in daylight from a treetop perch or while soaring, and its territorial and courtship display is a daytime aerial performance.

traits.defense.note: It leaves the perch and drops onto an approaching threat or intruder, and migrates and soars away from disturbance; Flee is the judgement mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: tolerant of settled areas and of people at a distance, but it will leave a perch or a nest tree and climb higher when approached closely.

habitat.use.note: The strong aerial share follows the perch-and-soar hunting described in the feeding section; the arboreal share covers the nest in a major fork of a large tree and the treetop perch; the small ground share covers walking to a kill and scavenging. The three shares are authored judgement.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the small_vertebrate tag is the schema's tag for the rodents and other small mammals that make up the bulk of the prey, and carrion covers the recorded scavenging and caching.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia states the species is not exclusively a bird of deep forest and can be found in suburban areas where houses or other buildings are mixed into woodlands, and in some residential areas in the West, and that it tends to live in stands with an open subcanopy.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'It is a permanent resident throughout most of its range, though northern birds do migrate, mostly to central Mexico', over distances of 300 to 1,500 km each way; winter_fraction is authored judgement at 0.4 for the share that migrates out of the northern breeding range.

seasonal.phases.note: Nest construction and reuse, clutch size, the 28-33 day incubation, asynchronous hatching, 40 days of brooding, nesting success, monogamy and the courtship displays are all stated in Wikipedia; the month bounds are authored judgement, as the article gives no calendar dates.

seasonal.life_stages.note: The article gives hatchling weight and 40 days of brooding but no fledging age or post-fledging dependency; the 70-day juvenile duration and the scale are authored judgement for a large raptor.

vocalizations.note: The screaming kee-aah call, its three-to-four repetitions and its use while courting or defending territories, and its imitation by Steller's jays and blue jays, are all from Wikipedia; the cooldown is authored judgement.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia: upper parts dark with pale spots, very long yellow legs, and a long tail by Buteo standards marked with narrow white bars; the species' name refers to the rusty-red shoulder. The shoulder patch, upperpart spotting and tail-bar parts are authored judgement to render the red shoulder, the pale spotting and the barred tail the description names; the yellow legs are drawn by colouring the mesh's own leg parts rather than by adding a part, which is how the earlier version of this record did it and which made an orange lump hang below the body in the perched pose; tail_ratio follows the stated tail length of 16-24 cm against a 38-61 cm body.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared seabird-predator program, which is the only shared aerial-predator program in the kit. Its states fit this species - patrol, hunt live prey, scavenge carrion, drink, flee, rest at shelter - and its prey tags are set to small_vertebrate and carrion, both of which this hawk genuinely uses, but the program's name and its water_within_m condition are written for a seabird and do not apply to a Buteo. A bespoke program would fit better; this was chosen over adding one because the fit is structural rather than nominal, and the compromise is recorded here. All radii are judgement, on the scale of a bird that hunts over a wide area and tolerates people at a distance.
